tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Invertible Differential Gives a Local Diffeomorphism]

↗ lem:smooth-local-inverse-on-open ↗ lem:invertible-operators-open

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F : M o N$ be smooth, and let $p$ be an interior point of $M$ at which $dF_p$ is invertible. Then $F$ is a local diffeomorphism at $p$: there are open sets $U i p$ and $V i F(p)$ such that $F|_U : U o V$ is a diffeomorphism.

Proof

↗ lem:smooth-local-inverse-on-open ↗ lem:invertible-operators-open Let $\varphi $ and $\psi $ be the charts of $M$ and $N$ around $p$ and $F(p)$, and let $g = \psi \circ F \circ \varphi ^{-1}$ be the coordinate representation of $F$, defined and smooth on the open set $\Omega $ of chart points whose image under $F$ lies in the domain of $\psi $. Because $p$ is an interior point, the chart image of a neighborhood of $p$ is a neighborhood of $a = \varphi (p)$ in the model space, so $dg_a$ is the ordinary differential of $g$ at $a$ and it is invertible, being $dF_p$ read in the charts.

Since $g$ is $C^\infty $ on $\Omega $, its differential $x \mapsto dg_x$ is continuous there, and by Lemma 5 the set of $x \in \Omega $ at which $dg_x$ is invertible is open. Shrinking, choose an open $s i a$ contained in $\Omega $ on which $dg_x$ is invertible for every $x \in s$. The inverse function theorem gives a local homeomorphism $R$ with $R = g$ near $a$; restrict it to $s$. Its inverse is $C^\infty $ on the open set $R(s)$ by Lemma 5, so $R$ restricted to $s$ is a diffeomorphism of $s$ onto the open set $R(s)$.

Conjugating back, $U = \varphi ^{-1}(s)$ and $V = \psi ^{-1}(R(s))$ are open, contain $p$ and $F(p)$ respectively, and $F|_U = \psi ^{-1} \circ R \circ \varphi $ is a composite of diffeomorphisms, hence a diffeomorphism onto $V$.

□

The most useful consequence of the inverse function theorem is the following. A smooth map $F: M o N$ is said to have constant rank if the linear map $dF_p$ has the same rank at every point $p \in M$.
